summary.intent: Design two new features for the memory-loop system: (1) memory editing with keyword-based injection triggers matched against user prompts, and (2) a user-configurable threshold setting to control how strictly/loosely the memory generation pipeline filters candidates.
summary.outcome: Requirements for keyword matching were clarified (keywords matched against user prompt at injection time). Three architectural options for the generation threshold were analyzed with pros/cons; no final decision was made — the session ended mid-discussion.

repo: Memory generation pipeline has three distinct filter layers: evidence gate (session count), confidence/strength floor (LLM-assigned values), and generic advice filter (phrase matching).
The evidence gate requiring 2+ sessions is the most impactful single filter in the generation pipeline.
LLM-assigned strength/confidence values are considered less reliable than session count as a quality signal.

implementation_rationale: Keywords matched at injection time (against user prompt) keeps the trigger mechanism explicit and predictable rather than relying solely on semantic similarity.
Combined dial (Option C) recommended because it maps directly to the user's stated mental model ('too loose / too strict') and avoids exposing internal filter complexity.
tradeoffs: Option A (evidence gate only): most impactful knob but doesn't address generic-advice or confidence filters.
Option B (confidence/strength floor only): allows weaker signals through but still blocked by evidence gate; LLM values are less reliable than session count.
Option C (combined dial): most user-friendly but less granular and harder to debug; proposed mitigation is per-gate escape hatches for power users.
codebase_patterns: Memory injection is gated at prompt-time, making keyword triggers a natural fit for the existing injection path.
Generation filtering is multi-layered (evidence gate + confidence floor + generic phrase filter) — any threshold setting must account for all three layers.
